reason: A reads left to right: hashtag badge, then a dominant '6 SYMPTOMS', then the list, doctor and CTA, so the hierarchy holds. But the symptom list is tiny and badly wrapped ('Sore throat Headache' merged on one line), and the doctor has shrunk to a cramped thumbnail beside the CTA. B shrinks the headline under a left-hand yellow block, jams the tiny CTA right against the symptom list so they nearly collide, and leaves the right third of the banner empty, making it lopsided and the CTA buried.

A pushes the whole T-and-text block into the top half, leaving roughly the bottom 45% as empty blue. Its red bar also stops short of the right edge, so it loses the original's bleed, and the stem stops floating mid-canvas instead of running to the bottom. B centres the block vertically and keeps the bar bleeding off the right edge as in the original, so it is more faithful and better balanced. But it is still the same small layout dropped into a tall canvas with large dead areas above and below. The stem is cut off mid-canvas, and the text is no bigger, so neither candidate actually rearranges the design for the story format.

A: the headline is shrunk to a small block. Its first line sits on the bottom edge of the T's crossbar, half on red and half on blue, which breaks the original's text-in-bar relationship. The tiny type leaves huge dead blue areas, so the copy no longer leads. B: it keeps the original structure: the first two lines sit inside the red crossbar, the rest runs down over the stem, and the type is large and legible. But everything is crammed into the left 65%, leaving the right third empty and lopsided. Lines like 'AGAINST CRUELTY' still straddle the red/blue edge, as they do in the original.

A breaks up the composition. The tree/MERRY/characters cluster is pushed left of centre and there is a large dead gap before the red monster, ghost and star monster, which are jammed against the right side. The bell is missing, the left edge is empty, and the headline is no longer centred. B keeps the original intact and centred, but it is just a shrunk copy: wide empty bands on both sides, a tiny 'DISCOUNT' headline, and nothing rearranged to fit the wide banner. Of the two, B is more coherent and on brand.

A breaks up the composition. The green heart ornament is cut off at the top edge, the main cluster is crammed into the top third, and the red monster, ghost and star monster are scattered down the right side with a huge empty area in the lower half. The tree monster's ladder and feet are also cut off at the bottom. B keeps the original arrangement intact, but it is just the landscape design shrunk into a band across the middle of the story canvas, leaving big empty areas above and below. The MERRY/DISCOUNT headline is small at this size and the characters are tiny. B needed rearranging, not shrinking, but it is still far better than A.

A and B look pixel-identical. In both, the photo is cropped so far into the fig that the cake and the actual dish are gone, leaving a blurry abstract strip. The 'Perfect Taste' wreath is shrunk to a small mid-canvas emblem, too small for its script text to read well at banner size, and it sits on a busy, low-contrast part of the photo. Most of the left side is dead blur, so the layout doesn't read left to right.

A: the mountain/hiker illustration is pushed against the left edge and stops at a hard vertical line around x=440, leaving the right half of the bottom empty and lopsided. The cross is also jammed between the invite copy and the dates, out of its original order, and a large dead gap sits above 'Worship & Bible Study'. B: the text stack keeps the original order and spacing and is well centred. Its flaw is that the illustration is centred but no longer full-bleed: the forest ends in hard vertical cuts on both sides, so the art reads as a cropped rectangle floating in pale margins.

A keeps the original's top-to-bottom order and a reasonably sized brick. But 'Buy 2 only for' and the price are indented (x≈45) while the headline and CTA sit at x≈18, so the left edges don't line up, and there is empty space to the right of the price and CTA. B shrinks the brick and X graphic to a small icon that barely registers. It also breaks 'Buy 2 / only / for' over three lines, leaving 'for' orphaned, sets the $14.99 price smaller than the offer copy, and floats a small ORDER NOW box off to the right where it competes with the offer.

Both leave a ~100px blank white strip on the left, so the building photo no longer bleeds off the left edge as in the original, which makes it look like a shrunk copy placed on the canvas. A is worse: its whole composition, including the off-white panel and headline, stops around x≈620, leaving a dead empty band on the right and lopsided balance. B pushes the right-aligned headline close to the right edge like the original and uses the width better, though the left gap still has to be fixed.

A: the headline, the URL and the 'HO SMART' wordmark are all missing. The white device logo is placed on a white background and barely shows, and the bottom 60% of the canvas is empty. Only the blue band and the phone photo survive as a recognisable top block. B: also loses all text. The blue slab floats in the middle with nothing in it, the photo is shrunk to a tiny strip next to a grey placeholder bar, and the oversized white-on-white logo is jammed against the right edge. That leaves B even more fragmented and empty than A.

A has lost the headline, URL and 'HO SMART' wordmark entirely. What's left is an empty floating blue parallelogram, a tiny squashed photo strip and a white logo outline that disappears on the white canvas, so it's unusable. Still, it keeps a recognisable blue header with the logo and an intact phone photo, though the white diagonal stripes spill awkwardly over the photo's left edge. That makes B the less broken of the two.

A: the headline is small and boxed into a heavy yellow/dark block on the left. The symptom list is tiny and runs into the CTA with almost no gutter ('Dry cough' nearly touches 'Call your doctor'), and the right third of the banner is empty, so it feels lopsided. B: it reads left to right with a strong hierarchy (hashtag badge, big '6 SYMPTOMS', list, doctor, yellow CTA), but the symptom list is still tiny with awkward merged lines, and the doctor illustration crowds right up against the CTA.

Both just place the original block onto the tall canvas without reworking it. In both, the red T stem stops in mid-air instead of bleeding off the bottom and top as it does in the original. B pushes everything into the top half and leaves the bottom ~330px empty, and its T bar ends short of the right edge, so 'NOW!' sits cramped against the bar's end. A keeps the original's text-on-T relationship and type scale, but the whole composition is jammed into the left ~60% of the canvas, leaving a large dead blue area on the right, and the stem crosses 'CRUELTY' and 'ANIMALS' unevenly. B centres the T but shrinks the headline badly for the canvas size. The first line also sits right on the bottom edge of the T's crossbar, half on red and half on blue, and 'NOW!' runs into the stem. A is just the original shrunk and centred. The whole composition sits in the middle third, leaving large empty dark bands on the left and right, and the MERRY/DISCOUNT headline is small for a banner. It keeps every element and its intended grouping, though. B breaks the composition: the headline and most characters crowd the left, while the red monster, ghost and star monster are pushed to the far right, leaving a large dead gap in between. The headline is off-centre and no longer the focal point, and the bell is lost.

A is the landscape layout shrunk into a band across the middle of the tall canvas. The top and bottom thirds are empty, and the MERRY/DISCOUNT headline and the characters are small. It keeps the composition intact but doesn't rearrange anything for the new shape. B falls apart: the heart ornament is cut off at the top edge, the star monster is cut off at the bottom, and the pink monster and ghost drift down the right edge. The cramped headline cluster sits beside a large empty area in the middle, so the layout has no balance or clear structure.

A and B look pixel-identical. In both, the 'Perfect Taste' lockup with its wreath is shrunk to a small centred badge, so the headline is undersized and has no presence in the leaderboard format. The photo is cropped to blurry fig fragments, so the cake hero is lost, and the left two-thirds of the banner is dead, blurred background instead of a left-to-right layout.

A keeps the original's centred text stack and reading order with good hierarchy. Its flaw is the mountain and forest illustration: it doesn't reach the canvas edges, so the tree silhouettes stop in hard vertical cuts at about x=110 and x=655, leaving bare strips at the sides. B's illustration is pushed to the left and cut off sharply at mid-canvas, which looks lopsided against the centred text. B also crams the cross up against the dates, putting it out of its original order, then leaves a large gap above 'Worship & Bible Study', so the spacing is uneven.

A shrinks the brick hero to a tiny thumbnail and leaves a large empty area to its right. 'Buy 2 only for' wraps badly, leaving 'for' alone on its own line. The $14.99 price is demoted to small text at the very bottom, and the ORDER NOW button floats unanchored on the right, so the price-to-action order is broken. B keeps the brick large and bleeding off the right edge like the original, and the price stays bold. Its flaws: the 'Buy 2 only for' and price block is indented about 25px from the headline's left edge (CTA and headline sit at about 18px), and there is dead space above the offer block.

Both leave the building photo starting about 100px in from the left, so there's a dead white strip on the left edge and the image no longer bleeds off the canvas as it does in the original. A at least keeps the headline right-aligned with a sensible right margin, close to the original. B has the same dead left strip, plus its headline sits on a white box that stops at about x=625, leaving a visible seam and an off-white band on the right. Its text also floats away from the right edge, so the layout looks unanchored.

Both lose all the text: no headline, no URL, no 'HO SMART' wordmark, so the message and brand are gone. A floats an empty blue slab in the middle, shrinks the hand photo into a tiny strip next to a grey placeholder bar, and sets a huge white device icon on white so it barely shows. B at least keeps the blue band at the top and a bigger photo, but the stripes run awkwardly over the photo, the icon is also white on white, and the bottom 60% of the canvas is empty.

A has no headline, 'HO SMART' wordmark or URL at all. The white device logo is clipped by the bottom edge of the blue band and half of it sits on white. The photo floats in a large empty white middle, and the diagonal stripes sit on top of the hand. B is worse: it also has no text, the blue parallelogram floats empty, the photo has shrunk to a tiny sliver, and the white logo sits on white, off-axis and practically invisible. A at least keeps the brand blue and the main photo at a size you can see.

A: the yellow hashtag band stops abruptly where it hits the doctor illustration, which sits on a stray white box. The symptom list merges items ('Shortness of breath Dry cough', 'Sore throat Headache'), the yellow CTA is tiny and crowded against the list, and the right end of the banner is empty. However, its list wraps badly ('Dry / cough') and still merges 'Sore throat Headache', the list text is very small, and the cropped doctor, sparkle and CTA are crammed together at the right edge.

A is a scaled-down copy of the original with no rearrangement: the geometric background does not fill the portrait canvas, which leaves large blank white bands at the top and bottom. The type block itself stays intact and readable. B has the same unfilled background, and its white frame is badly misplaced: the frame's top edge runs out into the blank white band above the pattern and its bottom edge cuts across the middle of the pattern. The text card is pushed up off-centre and the bottom half of the canvas is dead space, so B looks broken.

A keeps the T recognisable, with the stem centred under the bar and the headline intact. But the shrunken group sits off to the left and leaves the right ~45% of the canvas as dead blue space; the T no longer bleeds off the edges as in the original; and the white copy runs across the stem edge raggedly. B centres the group, which balances the space better, but it orphans 'NOW!' on its own line inside the red bar. The stem is pushed to the bar's right end, so the T reads as a Γ/L shape. The red block also clips oddly behind the white lines, which damages both the brand mark and the headline.

A is a shrunken copy of the square design dropped left of centre. Large empty blue areas sit on both sides, and the T stem stops just short of the bottom edge instead of bleeding off it, so the banner shape goes unused, but the headline's line breaks and the text-to-T relationship survive. B has the same small, centred, dead-space problem and is worse: 'NOW!' is orphaned on its own line, which breaks the headline's first line apart, and 'TO ANIMALS' straddles the red/blue stem edge more awkwardly.

A keeps the photos and the headline frame, but the top half is a squashed copy of the original. The bottom half is mostly dead white space, and the plate sketch, Cascadia, RESTAURANT and the URL fall outside the frame in a loose column down the left edge. The tall frame is also mostly empty under the headline. B is unusable: both food photos have shrunk to tiny thumbnails inside the pattern tiles. A: the headline reads clearly at the left, but the decorative O, X and lines have been blown up into a large meaningless cluster in the middle that competes with the message. A breaks the diamond collage: a rectangular photo strip at the right edge runs down to the text zone. It is still coherent and on brand, so it is less bad than A.

In A, the forest background only fills a centre strip and leaves white bands on both sides. A breaks the stripe motif. The grey, blue and red bands have odd white gaps between them and all stop at about y=675, leaving a dead white strip along the bottom. Both keep the original's three-column structure (headline, window, details), but the stained-glass window is much smaller and no longer the strong centrepiece it was. A keeps the stained-glass window clear of the edges with even top and bottom margins and keeps the original's three-column structure. B has a larger, more readable headline and details, but the window runs almost edge to edge, jammed against the top and bottom of the canvas so it looks cropped. That breaks the original's breathing room and makes the centre feel cramped next to wide empty sides.

A: the headline reads as the broken phrase 'CONS TRUC TION' on one line. The key brick-and-X imagery has shrunk to a tiny thumbnail jammed in the top-right corner. A: the robot vacuum is cropped into a blurry, unrecognisable close-up. A: nothing collides, but the illustration clusters are shrunk and float in the middle with a hard, straight cropped bottom edge. A: the illustration clusters have shrunk to tiny thumbnails pushed against the left and right edges, and 'CREATIVE AGENCY' sits about 200 px below 'CLAYTONI', leaving large dead navy areas, so the title and its tagline no longer read as one lockup. A reads left to right as a banner should: hashtag chip, then a dominant '6 SYMPTOMS', list, doctor, CTA. A is broken. The geometric background stops partway down the portrait canvas, which leaves big white bands at the top and bottom. A: the T is shrunk to a floating, centred block with wide empty blue on both sides. It loses the original's edge-bleeding T. Neither candidate rearranges the layout for the banner. A is broken. A: the maroon panel has come loose from the copy and sits empty on the left as a meaningless square. A is just the portrait original shrunk into the centre of a wide canvas. A: the forest background covers only a narrow centre strip, with white space on both sides. A is not a real resize. It pastes the original portrait layout onto the square canvas without rearranging anything. The red stripe stops short and leaves an odd white strip on the right, there is a large empty white area on the left, and the stripes and card are pushed off-centre, though the card, text and stripe colours survive intact. B breaks the structure: the stripes stop at about 88% of the height and leave a dead white band at the bottom, uneven white gaps split the stripes apart, the card has lost its bottom edge and merges into the band, and 'TRAVEL MUGS' sits jammed against where the stripes end.

Both use the same faithful three-column banner. In both, the stained-glass window has shrunk into a small icon that no longer anchors the design, and the address is at small-print size. A's headline is bigger, but it crowds the top and left edges, and the date/address block almost touches the right edge, so the side margins are tight and uneven. B has more even margins on all sides and a calmer balance, but its headline is a little smaller and the gutters between the three columns are not consistent.

A keeps the original three-part left/centre/right structure and holds text at a readable size. However, the stained-glass window runs almost the full canvas height, with nearly no top or bottom margin, so the middle feels cramped. B gives the window better breathing room, but it shrinks both the headline and the date/address block too far. The fine print is barely legible at banner size, and the elements float in a lot of empty white space, which weakens the hierarchy.

A keeps the brick-and-X hero at a strong size and reads in a sensible left-to-right order: headline, product, offer, price, CTA. It has clear flaws, though. 'Sets for kids' is jammed right up against the stacked 'CONS/TRUC/TION' headline, and 'Buy 2 only for' almost touches the X. The left margin is a dead area, and the headline is still split into word fragments. B is worse. It sets the headline on one line as 'CONS TRUC TION' with spaces, which reads as broken words. The key product image shrinks to a tiny icon jammed into the top-right corner. The price comes after the ORDER NOW button and is squeezed against the right edge, which breaks the reading order, and the right half is a scattered cluster with uneven spacing.

A: the robot vacuum is cropped so tightly that the product can't be recognised, and the purple circle ends in a hard vertical cut that looks like a mistake. Oversized dot grids sit over the product photo, and the outline frame floats at random in the middle of the image. The 'Smart Home' text is smaller and the whole group is pushed into the right corner, so B is the messier of the two.

Both candidates have the same layout and both are broken. The building photo has shrunk to a thin cropped sliver, so the original's key image is lost, and the 'the limit' line sits directly on top of it, which is the kind of unwanted collision the brief forbids. A's headline starts right under the top edge and leaves a large empty band at the bottom. B's text sits a little lower, which balances the canvas slightly better, but it has the same image collision and the same bottom-heavy empty space.

A: the CLAYTONI headline is blown up so far that it runs into both illustration clusters, so the letters sit on busy artwork. However, the illustrations still have the same hard-cropped bottom edge and float in a band with dead space above, and the subhead drifts low, leaving a loose gap below the headline.

A: 'CLAYTONI' is pushed to the top edge and 'CREATIVE AGENCY' to the bottom, about 500px apart, so the lockup is broken. The illustration clusters have shrunk to tiny stamps floating mid-canvas with huge dead navy areas above and below. The tagline also sits far below with lots of empty space, and the top third is empty. Neither one rearranges the artwork for the tall format.

A keeps GET A GIFT as the dominant element and splits brand, headline and offer into sensible banner columns, but the dashed divider rules are scattered loose in the left column, the LYGOM CAFE logo and www.lygom.se are tiny, and the left-hand stack is cramped against the canvas edge. The gift icons are oversized, 'Only this Christmas' and the stars sit on the photo, and two full-width dashed lines run across the bottom for no reason, so B is unusable.

Both crops lose the key imagery: the heart mug and red gift are cut to slivers at the right edge. In A, the 'A GIFT' headline and the dashed dividers run onto the sweater photo, so text sits on a busy image. A also has a stray rule floating under LYGOM CAFE, oversized stars and a large dead gap above 'Only this Christmas'. B keeps all text on the pink field with clean hierarchy, but its type is undersized for the tall format (the website and 'Only this Christmas' are small). B also has extra detached divider lines around the tagline and wastes space at top and bottom.

A: the photo is centred with even margins and the headline and URL are centred and readable. But the white cross that framed the text in the original is now a huge empty outline floating in white space. The text sits below it instead of inside, so the cross is a meaningless dead shape taking up a third of the canvas. B: the headline does sit in the cross as in the original, and it is larger. But the photo is jammed against the top-left edges with an odd empty strip on the right. There is a big blank gap between the photo and the cross, the cross is cut off by the bottom edge, and the URL sits cramped near the bottom. Overall B looks more broken.

A is just the original shrunk into the left half: the right ~45% of the banner is empty grey, the text is small, and the layout is badly lopsided. Still, the red panel, quote, attribution and skyline keep their original relationships. B fills the canvas but breaks the design: a decorative line cuts through 'MODERN' in the headline, the bottom half of the red panel is empty, the attribution floats off to the side, and the skyline becomes a small separate thumbnail in a white box, so the signature skyline-over-panel image is lost.

I rated both candidates 2 out of 5 and picked B as less bad. A spreads the elements unevenly. The MERRY/DISCOUNT headline is pushed left of centre and is small, and there is a large dead gap between the headline group and the right-hand monsters. The bell sits on top of the green heart creature, and the holly is jammed against the red monster. B keeps the original composition and centres the headline. However, it is just a shrunk copy in a central block. It leaves wide empty strips on both sides, the headline is tiny for a banner, and the ladder monster is cut off at the bottom edge.

A and B are the same image as far as I can see. In both, the 'Perfect Taste' wordmark and its gold wreath are shrunk to a tiny centred badge that barely reads on the strip. The photo is cropped to blurry, unrecognisable slices of fig with no tart showing, and the empty left half wastes the left-to-right banner shape, so it looks like a shrunk copy rather than a rearranged design.

A works as a banner. The large headline is set left with good margins and the cat illustration is anchored at the bottom right, so it reads left to right. Its flaws are small: the cat group is a bit small, which leaves a slightly loose gap between the text and the cats. B shrinks the headline, so it loses dominance, and jams it against the left edge. The cat group floats in from the right, leaving about 130px of empty purple on the right side, so the layout feels lopsided and arbitrary.

Both keep the original's three-column left-to-right structure, which suits the leaderboard banner. In both, the stained-glass window shrinks to a small icon with large empty gaps on either side, and the event details are tiny at this size. A's headline and details are slightly larger and easier to read, though the headline sits close to the top edge. In B, the text is smaller and the window nearly touches the bottom edge, so the date and address are harder to read.

A puts the red 'EVENT MANAGMENT' eyebrow below the headline and left-aligned against a centered headline, which breaks both reading order and alignment. Its brown owl is blown up into a centered focal point that competes with the headline, the blue owl is shrunk to a tiny afterthought jammed into the bottom-left corner, and the confetti is clipped into a band with a large empty area beneath. B keeps the original structure: hanging owl at the top, eyebrow above a dominant centered headline, blue owl anchoring the bottom. Its flaws are confetti stars sitting on and around the headline letters, and the confetti field visibly cut off as a strip at its top edge.

A keeps the original's hierarchy, with the stacked headline, then the price, then the CTA, but the left edges don't line up: the headline sits at about x=27, 'Buy 2' at about x=80, the price at about 60 and the button at about 44. The brick and X are also cut off with a hard edge around x=400 instead of at the canvas edge. B shrinks the headline to a tiny 'CONS TRUC TION', which is unreadable as one word, and blows the brick up until it is pixelated and clipped. It also squeezes 'Buy 2 only for', the price and the CTA into one tiny footer row, so the offer and the call to action get lost.

A is broken. The 'with your next cup of coffee' subhead is huge and sits right on the busy sweater photo, while 'GET A GIFT' has shrunk to a small caption, so the hierarchy is upside down. 'Only this Christmas' and the stars also collide with the photo, and the dashed dividers run through the image. B keeps the headline dominant and crops the photo cleanly with no text on it, but the left column is cramped and ragged: the logo/gift block and the copy block sit on different axes, the dashed rules are misaligned and of uneven length, the stars are oversized, and the URL is tiny.

A: the type is too small for a story format (the headline fills less than half the column), the vertical gaps are uneven and stretched, extra rules were added around 'Only this Christmas', and the photo crop cuts off the heart mug and gift at the right edge, losing the key product image. B: the larger headline 'A GIFT' and the dashed rule run into the sweater sleeve, putting text over a busy image; there is a stray extra rule under the logo, the stars are oversized and compete with the copy, and the mug and gift are still cropped off.

A: the photo sits off-centre. It touches the top and left edges and leaves a gap on the right. Below it is a big dead white band, and the X outline runs off the bottom and sides of the canvas. The headline does stay inside the X as in the original, but the X is now white on white, so it no longer reads as a shape. B: the photo is inset with even margins and keeps its proportions. However, the X outline is left completely empty as a large meaningless shape in the middle, and the headline and URL sit below it, cut off from the motif. The headline is also smaller and weaker than in A. Both fall short, but B's framing is cleaner.

A breaks the design apart. The red quote panel's lower half is empty. The skyline is shrunk to a small thumbnail floating in a separate white box on the right, so it no longer anchors the text. A stray decorative line runs under 'MODERN', and the author name drifts off to the side of the quote. B is the original shrunk unchanged into the left half of the canvas, leaving the right half as dead grey space and the text small. B is still the less bad of the two because it keeps the original composition and its skyline-over-quote feel.

A is just the original shrunk and centred: about a quarter of the canvas on each side is empty, and the MERRY/DISCOUNT headline is small and weak for a banner, but the composition, hierarchy and all illustrations survive intact. B spreads the elements but is lopsided. The headline sits off-centre to the left with a large empty hole in the middle right. The heart creature and holly are cropped at the top edge, and the bell is lost. The headline is even smaller than in A, so the focal point is weakened.

A and B look pixel-identical. In both, the background is cropped to a blurry, meaningless strip of fig and dark backdrop, so the hero food image is lost. The 'Perfect Taste' wreath is shrunk to a tiny badge in the middle, with a lot of dead space on the left and right. That headline is barely legible at this size and sits on the busy fig edge on the right. Neither candidate rearranges the layout for the wide banner shape.

A: the headline is undersized and sits tight to the left edge (about 18px margin). The cat illustration crowds right up against 'AND', leaving almost no gutter, and about 130px of dead purple space is left at the far right, so the layout feels lopsided. B: the headline is larger and sits in the left block with more even margins and a clear gap before the art. The cats are shrunk a bit too much and pushed into the bottom-right corner, leaving empty space above them and making the key imagery feel minor next to the text. Even so, B's hierarchy and spacing are cleaner overall.

Both use the same three-column banner and keep the brand, but the window is pushed to the centre, leaving big empty gaps on either side. In the original it sat tight against the headline. In both, the date and address lines on the right are tiny and hard to read at this height. A's window almost touches the top and bottom edges, and its headline is a little smaller. B's headline is slightly larger and its window has a little more breathing room, so B is marginally better.

A keeps the original structure: the hanging owl at the top, the centered 'EVENT MANAGMENT' eyebrow, then the headline, then the blue owl at the bottom. Its flaws are confetti squeezed into one band that runs behind the headline letters, the bottom owl cropped hard at the edge, and empty gaps around the text block. B has the wrong reading order, with the eyebrow placed below the headline and left-aligned while the headline is centered. The hanging owl floats in the middle, cut off flat at the top, and the blue owl is shrunk to a tiny corner icon, so the pair of owls no longer balances and there is a large empty area below.

A: Hierarchy is wrong. The headline is shrunk to a small single line, "CONS TRUC TION", with odd gaps. A huge, pixelated brick takes over the canvas. "Buy 2 only for", the $14.99 price and ORDER NOW are tiny and squeezed into one bottom row, with the button between the copy and its price, which breaks the reading order. B: Keeps the original's top-to-bottom stack with a strong headline and a clear price/CTA. However, the Buy 2/price/CTA block is indented and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge. The brick is cut off at the right edge and slightly soft. There is uneven empty space between the brick and the offer block.

A is just the original shrunk and centred, with large blank white bars down both sides. Nothing was rearranged for the wide format, the orange header and photo end abruptly at the bars, and the photo is cropped at the bottom. Even so, it is balanced and intact. B makes the same shrink-without-redesign mistake but pins the design to the left, leaving about a third of the canvas on the right empty, so the layout is badly lopsided and plainly unfinished.

A shoves everything to the left, leaving the right third of the canvas dead white. The watercolour texture ends in a hard vertical edge at about x=595, and the barrel photo is narrower than the texture beneath it, so the two layers don't line up and the layout looks broken and lopsided. B keeps the original stack centred, so it is coherent and readable, but it is just the square design shrunk and boxed between empty white side margins with no reflow for the wide format. The texture also sticks out past the photo's left edge, and the logo, wordmark and tagline stay small in the wide canvas.

A: the symptom list is tiny and run together into paragraph-like lines ('Shortness of breath Dry cough', 'Sore throat Headache' on one line), so it no longer reads as a list. The hashtag is shrunk into an inset chip, the CTA is near-illegible fine print, and there are dead gaps above and below the doctor. B: the list keeps its stacked structure at a readable size, and the headline → illustration → list → CTA order works for a skyscraper. But the yellow hashtag bar is cut off at half width and jammed into the corner, the list is crammed against the CTA, and the CTA sits too close to the bottom edge.

In A, the stacked 'Spa Utopia' headline is tiny and barely stands out. 'Weekly SPA items review' sits on the glass jar and leaves, so it is low-contrast, almost as large as the headline, and hard to read. The tagline also drifts far from the headline, so the two don't read as one group. In B, the one-line 'Spa Utopia' headline is large and reads clearly as the main message, but the 'S' collides with the green bottle and the line runs across the glass dish. The tagline breaks awkwardly into 'Weekly SPA / items review' and sits on busy leaves, where it is nearly illegible. B is less bad because its hierarchy is clearer.

A: the photo collage is squeezed into a cramped left block, the '12641 Fenix Ave' text is tiny, and the date diamond sits right up against the body copy. The headline rule has drifted to the top-right corner, away from the headline, and a large empty band runs from x≈500 to 700. B: the headline is larger and fills the banner width, giving it a clear left-to-right flow. Its problems are a faint lattice of white diamonds floating in the middle, a headline rule left stranded under that lattice instead of under the headline, and an address and vertical URL too small to read.

A is broken. The pink subhead sits above the headline and breaks lines badly ('YOU CANNOT' / 'VIRTUAL' left orphaned). 'IT'S TIME FOR THEM TO BECOME REAL.' is squeezed into a narrow column with one word per line, the event details are shrunk until they can't be read, and the text pieces are scattered with no grid. B keeps the original reading order and type sizes in a sensible two-column layout, but it has clear flaws: the pink square nearly touches the subhead, the icons are small and float on the left, the URL is centred while the text above it is left-aligned, and a large empty band runs along the bottom.

In A, the green background is a narrow centred strip on a white canvas, so the oversized white headline and subline run off it onto white and become unreadable ('Event Devo', 'ernational D', 'ration & Forest clea'). The quote and URL are missing, and one divider floats off to the right. B has the same broken strip background, and its headline, subline and quote are also cut off where they spill onto white, with both dividers stranded on the right. B is slightly less bad because it keeps more of the content, and the URL and part of the copy are still readable. Neither could ship.

A breaks up the stripe motif: the grey and blue stripes float as unrelated bars, and the stripes stop at about y=380, leaving a dead white band along the bottom. The white card merges with the white background, so it no longer reads as a panel. It also cuts an odd notch into the red stripe, and 'TRAVEL MUGS' is jammed against the bottom edge where the stripes end, so the layout looks broken. B keeps the original stripes and card intact, so the brand survives, but it is just a shrunk copy centred in the banner with large empty white areas on both sides. Its body text and list are tiny, and it has not been rearranged for the wide format.

A: the headline sits only about 15px from the left edge. The cat cluster is too small and floats mid-right, leaving a dead purple strip of about 150px on the right edge, so the weight looks lopsided and the canvas underused. B: the headline is larger and has a better left margin. The cats are anchored to the bottom-right corner as in the original, which gives a balanced left-to-right banner, but the cats crowd the right edge and the gap between the text and the illustration is slightly tight.

A pushes the whole column to the left so the right ~45% of the canvas is dead space. The divider line sits at x≈203, well right of the text's centre axis (~156), and the rose is cut off with a hard vertical edge at the left and right sides. B keeps the text, divider and rose on one centred axis, but it just drops the narrow original into the middle of the wider canvas: the rose has visibly hard clipped vertical edges, the side margins are empty, and nothing was rearranged for the new shape.

A turns the headline into 'CONS TRUC TION' on one line with spaces, so the word reads as three broken fragments. Its elements are scattered to the corners with big dead areas in between, and the CTA sits between 'Buy 2 only for' and '$14.99', which splits the price message and breaks the reading order. B keeps the original's stacked headline, copy grouping and price-to-CTA flow. Its flaws: the brick and the blue X are cut off sharply in the middle of the canvas instead of at an edge, 'Sets for kids' sits jammed against the brick, and the whole layout clusters in the centre-left, leaving the right third empty.

A: the image strip is not extended into the taller canvas, so empty white bands sit above and below it, and the 't' of 'the' just touches the tip of the building image (in the original the headline stays clear of it). B has the same empty top and bottom bands, and its larger headline pushes 'the limit' well into the striped building photo, so the text sits on a busy image. That collision is worse than A's slight touch.

A is the original scaled down and pushed against the left edge, leaving about a third of the canvas as empty white on the right, so it is lopsided and clearly unfinished. B is the same unchanged shrink, centred with blank white bars on both sides. It is balanced but still letterboxed, with nothing rearranged for the wide format, and the small 'HOW TO LEVEL UP'/search-bar headline doesn't make use of the extra width.

A is just the original scaled and centred, which leaves wide dead white columns on both sides, so it looks pillarboxed rather than redesigned for the wide banner format. It is still coherent and close to the original. B is broken: the barrel photo is shoved to the left and ends abruptly at x≈415, while the watercolour wash runs further right and then stops with a hard edge at x≈595. The logo, title and tagline sit off-centre (about x≈298 on a 768-wide canvas), and the right ~170px is empty, so the layout is lopsided.

A: the hashtag bar is clipped to an odd partial-width box flush against the top-left. The symptom list and CTA are jammed into the bottom third with almost no margin to the canvas edge, "cough" is orphaned, and the list text nearly matches the headline in size. B: the symptom list is tiny and its line breaks are destroyed ("Sore throat Headache" runs together on one line, "Shortness of breath Dry / cough"), so it no longer reads as a list. Its spacing is uneven, with dead gaps between blocks, though the hashtag badge and CTA margins are cleaner. A is more readable, so it is the less bad of the two.

A: 'Spa Utopia' is set on one line at a strong size, so the hierarchy holds. But the 'S' collides with the green dropper bottle, and the subline 'Weekly SPA items review' wraps into two tiny lines over the busy leaves, where it is barely legible. B: the headline shrinks to a tiny two-line stack that hardly outweighs the subline, so the hierarchy collapses. The subline also runs straight across the glass jar and the leaves, so the text sits on a busy image and is hard to read.

A: the headline is large and strong, and both diamond badges sit cleanly on a rectangular photo crop. But the diamond-grid mask has come away from the photo and floats as faint white lines over empty white space. The headline's underline is stranded at the bottom left, away from the headline, and the URL is microscopic. B: the photo mask is ragged and the white diamonds leave chopped holes. The date diamond hangs off the photo edge into the text area. The underline floats alone in the top right. The headline is undersized, and about a third of the canvas on the right is empty, which makes the layout lopsided.

A uses a sensible two-column banner, but the pink square almost touches the pink subtitle, the URL is centred while the other text is left-aligned, the icons are small and floating, and there is dead space along the bottom. B is broken: 'IT'S TIME FOR THEM TO BECOME REAL' is squeezed into a narrow stack with one word per line, the event details are too small to read, the subtitle has awkward breaks ('YOU CANNOT' / 'VIRTUAL'), and the headline sits below the subtitle, which jumbles the reading order.

A: the forest background covers only a narrow centre strip and the rest of the canvas is white. The white headline, subhead and body copy spill onto that white and disappear ('ent Devoted', 'ational Day'), the cream divider lines float off to the right, and 'March 21' sits on pale sky with almost no contrast. Even so, the URL and parts of the body copy can still be read. B has the same broken strip background with the headline enlarged and cut off worse ('Event Devo', 'ernational D'), the subhead cut off on both sides, a stray divider, and the quote and URL lines missing entirely, so it loses more content than A.

A is just the original shrunk and centred on the landscape canvas. Big dead white areas sit on both sides, nothing is rearranged for the banner shape, and the list and 'for all drinkware on' text are tiny, but the stripes, white card and hierarchy are still intact. B breaks the design: the grey, blue and red stripes are pulled apart with white gaps between them and stop short of the bottom edge, leaving a white band. The white card blends into the background so it disappears, the red stripe has a strange notch, and the copy block is jammed against the right edge.

A is a sensible left-to-right banner with the headline dominant and the cat cluster on the right edge, but the cats are shrunk small, the orange cat's ears nearly touch the top edge, and the gap between the headline and the cats is tight. B shrinks the headline, crams it against the left edge with almost no gap before the cats, and leaves a dead strip of empty purple on the right, so the layout is lopsided and the headline loses its dominance.

A keeps the centred axis and the reading order, but it is just the narrow original column placed in the middle of a wider canvas. The rose's hard vertical crop edges float in open white space, the copy stays small, and wide blank margins sit on both sides, so nothing was rearranged for the format. B is worse: the text block shifts left while the divider line stays off-centre, so the shared axis breaks. The rose is jammed against the left edge with a visible hard cut on its right side, and the whole right half is dead space, which makes the layout badly lopsided.

A keeps the stacked CONS/TRUC/TION headline, the brick and the price/CTA group in a sensible left-to-right flow. However, everything is packed into a central cluster with wide empty margins on the left and right. 'Sets for kids' sits jammed against the brick. The brick and X are clipped hard on their right side, and the left and right columns don't share a top or bottom edge. B breaks the headline into 'CONS TRUC TION', with odd spaces in a single word. It scatters 'Sets for kids', 'Buy 2 only for' and '$14.99' into the far corners. The ORDER NOW button sits between 'Buy 2 only for' and its price, which breaks the reading order, and the subordinate copy is about as prominent as the price.

A: the headline is blown up so far that 'the limit' runs about 90 px into the busy striped building photo, and 'us.' sits tight against the right edge. In both, the photo is a short letterboxed strip with empty white bands above and below, so the layout looks like the original pasted onto a taller canvas rather than rearranged for it. B: same letterboxed photo and dead space, but the headline stays close to its original size and only 'the' clips the tip of the image, so the collision is much smaller and the margins hold.
